one_line: Right verdict 'not ready' for the right main reason (no tracks, 2 unconnected: GND and RESET), 0 DRC errors not mistaken for a wired board, library/silkscreen warnings kept apart from copper, layers/outline/drills/fab-sheet numbers right, a 11-file gerber+drill zip delivered; but it calls the 0.2 mm clearance 'unverified', turns ERC power-flag errors into blockers and invents a 'purpose undefined' blocker, and the board picture is a bare pad plot.

holdout_leakage.why_right: General guidance plus tool output. eng-pcb-review says: a clean DRC is not proof, run pcb_erc, ask for the fab sheet, library noise is separate, `unconnected_count` 0 means every net is routed, ask whose board it is. The assistant checked `unconnected` on its own and reported the two pairs from the tool's list. The skill's worked examples are another board (pic_programmer, 160 x 99.1 mm) so nothing was copied from this scenario. The 'DRC error_count 0 but 2 unconnected' split comes from the tool output only; the skill does not say that error_count excludes unconnected, which is why turn 1 and turn 2 disagree on 'errors'.
holdout_leakage.luck_or_trap: No trap fallen into on the central question. The assistant did not say 'ready'; the 'DRC 0 errors means wired' belief was corrected twice. One partial trap: the clearance row was labelled 'unverified' although DRC had actually checked pad-to-pad clearance (truth: tightest copper gap 0.84 mm, 0.2 mm met).
holdout_leakage.leak_check: grep of the skill text for Arduino_Nano, 43.18, 1.651 finds nothing in the pcb skill.

goal_met_note: Straight no with reasons, layers (2), outline (43.18 x 17.78), drills (30 x 1.0 PTH, 4 x 1.651 NPTH) checked against the fab sheet, a zip of 9 gerber layers + job file + drill file, and a picture of the board. The fab-clearance row is reported as 'no violation but not verified'.

traps.trap: '0 DRC errors' read as a finished, wired board
library / silkscreen warnings called copper violations
traps.note: Not fallen into: library warnings were set aside as noise and the 5 silkscreen items were shown as warnings, never as copper faults. Marked false only because the field means 'fell into'; read as: trap avoided.

traps.trap: clearance verdict: pads-only board still meets 0.2 mm

honesty.issue: States 'the 0.2 mm clearance is unverified because there are no tracks'. pcb_drc checked copper clearance between the pads at 0.2 mm and found nothing; the assistant had no measured gap, so it should say 'met by DRC (pads only), margin not reported'. It understates, so this is a false caution, not a false pass.

Turn 1 says 'actually 2 errors' while the tool's error_count is 0; corrected in turn 2 with the explanation that unconnected is counted separately. The first wording confused a non-expert user (she asked why 0 errors and 2 errors).

Blocker 2 ('power source missing') and blocker 3 ('purpose undefined, the senior must say') are inference presented as findings; on a header-only breakout template, power_pin_not_driven means no PWR_FLAG / no output pin on the power nets, not that the board needs a regulator. The assistant did mark the 26 single-pad nets as 'not verified against the pin table'.
Unverified claim labelled correctly: 'drl hashes differ, cause not verified, probably timestamp'.

pictures.notes: Harness rasterisation of the PDF the assistant exported (the tool has no PNG). Outline, 30 blue pads (pin 1 square), 4 black mounting holes. No net names, no pad numbers, no airwires for the 2 missing connections, no scale. Correct and legible, but the person's reaction 'only circles, no lines' shows it answers nothing about readiness; the assistant described it accurately in words (also read the PDF with Read).
Same picture, a second rendering of the same PDF (harness duplicate).

problems.what: pcb_drc returns error_count 0 and, separately, unconnected_count 2; there is no combined 'blocking items' count and no measured minimum clearance, so the model both calls the unconnected pairs 'errors' and cannot state the clearance margin for the fab check.
problems.evidence: pcb_drc result: values error_count 0, unconnected_count 2, violation_count 11; data.rule_set overrides_mm clearance 0.2; no field for the tightest gap.
problems.fix: pcb_drc: add `blocking_count` (errors + unconnected) and `data.measured` with the smallest copper-to-copper gap and smallest track width found; the skill then lets the checklist row read 'min gap 0.84 mm vs 0.2 mm, margin 0.64'.

problems.what: eng-pcb-review explains `unconnected_count 0` but not what a non-zero one means for the verdict, nor that error_count excludes unconnected, nor that pads-only boards still get a clearance check (pad-to-pad). The assistant wrote 'unverified' for clearance and elevated ERC power_pin_not_driven to a blocker.
problems.evidence: SKILL.md section 4 item 4 only covers the 0 case; turn 1 and turn 5 clearance row 'unverified'.
problems.fix: Add to section 4: 'unconnected_count > 0 means unrouted nets: list the pairs, not ready, error_count does not include them. Pad-to-pad clearance is checked even with no tracks: report as met with the DRC rule used. power_pin_not_driven on a connector-only schematic is a missing power flag; report it as schematic-level, not as a fab blocker'.

problems.what: Turn 3 headline: 'the missing connections are not only GND and RESET' followed by a table showing only those two; the person asked exactly that question. Also opened with 'which board is yours?' when she had said these are the files.
problems.evidence: Turn 3 first bold sentence vs its table.
problems.fix: None needed in tools; a skill sentence on answering the literal question first would help.

problems.what: No board picture tool: pcb_export pdf/svg only, layers overlaid, no pad names, no ratsnest. The person asked for a picture of the board; what she got cannot show that two connections are missing.
problems.evidence: Both rendered PNGs: pads and holes only; persona: 'why only circles, no lines'. Skill section 5: 'no PNG export'.
problems.fix: pcb_export/pcb_info: a `view` option that draws pads with net names, courtyards, and airwires for unconnected pairs (PNG, with a legend), or at least colour the unrouted pads.

problems.what: pcb_export has no inline_image and the PDF path was the only hand-over; the person saw the picture only because the harness rasterised it. The path was given in words. Zip content (11 entries) matches what the assistant listed.
problems.evidence: No tool PNG in ws/; rendered/ holds harness PNGs of the PDF.
problems.fix: Harness: record tool-result image blocks; pcb_export: optional PNG render.

problems.what: Truth's gerber list (22 files) differs from the tool's 11-entry zip (no courtyard/fab/adhesive/user layers); the tool's subset is what a fab needs, so this is not a product defect. The person asked ('where is my picture') before any export was offered because turn 1 had said 'gerber not run'.

what_worked: Loaded eng-pcb-review (and eng-toolkit) before the first tool call and followed it: pcb_info for layers/outline, pcb_drc with the person's 0.2 mm, pcb_erc on the schematic, library warnings reported as noise, honest 'unreviewed' limit.
Did not say ready. Told her the files are KiCad's own template, that tracks/vias/zones are 0, and corrected itself in turn 2 about 'errors' vs unconnected.
Drill sizes were read from the actual .drl, split plated/non-plated, and compared with her fab sheet row by row, with 'not on the sheet' items (annular ring, mask) named as not checked.
Delivered the zip with a correct description of its content, plus a plain next step (ask the senior for fab name and board function).
